official_sources.title: Council of Europe – Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR)

units.title: Alphabet, Sounds, Greetings, and Introductions
units.scenario: You arrive at a language course in Berlin, learn how German writing maps to sound, spell your name, and meet classmates and the teacher.
units.can_do: I can recognize the German alphabet and its extra characters, pronounce core sound patterns, spell my name, greet people, and exchange names and origins.

foundations.title: The German alphabet and letter names
foundations.explanation: German starts with the same 26 Latin letters as English and adds Ä, Ö, Ü, and ß. The letter names are: A ah, B beh, C tseh, D deh, E eh, F eff, G geh, H hah, I ee, J yot, K kah, L ell, M emm, N enn, O oh, P peh, Q koo, R err, S ess, T teh, U oo, V fow, W veh, X iks, Y üpsilon, Z tsett. In spelling, ß is called Eszett and the umlauted vowels are named Ä, Ö, and Ü.
foundations.practice: Point to and say every letter in order, then spell your first and last name aloud twice: once slowly and once at a natural pace.

foundations.title: Letters are instructions for sound
foundations.explanation: German spelling is comparatively systematic. Start with a few dependable mappings: ei sounds like English eye, ie is a long ee, eu and äu sound like oy, j sounds like English y, w sounds like English v, and z begins with a ts sound. The letters ch change with their vowel environment, so learn ich and Buch as two anchor words rather than forcing one English sound onto both.
foundations.practice: Read mein, Sie, heute, ja, Wasser, zehn, ich, and Buch aloud; underline the letter group that tells you the key sound in each word.

foundations.title: Build a sentence around the verb
foundations.explanation: A basic German statement has a subject and a conjugated verb, with the verb normally in position two: Ich heiße Maria; Ich komme aus Spanien. A basic question changes either the question word or the order, but the verb remains the engine that connects the person to the information.
foundations.practice: Keep Ich fixed and swap heiße, bin, and komme aus; then replace Ich with Sie and notice which verb form must change.

grammar: German letter names and core sound-spelling correspondences

dialogue.speaker: Lehrerin
dialogue.translation: Good morning! What is your name?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Nice to meet you too!

pronunciation: German 'ch' in 'ich' is a soft palatal sound, while 'ch' in 'Buch' is formed farther back; neither is English 'k'.
Letter names differ from English: J is 'yot', W is 'veh', V is 'fow', and Z is 'tsett'.
units.pragmatics: Use Sie until invited to duzen. Teachers often use Sie first; peers switch to du quickly.
units.culture: Germans shake hands in formal introductions and state their full name clearly.
units.speaking_prompt: Introduce yourself: name, origin, and a polite closing.
units.writing_prompt: Write six sentences: greeting, name, origin, and goodbye.

checks.explanation: The German name of Z is 'tsett'; this sound anchor helps when spelling names and addresses.

checks.prompt: Sie hören: 'Auf Wiedersehen!' Was antworten Sie?

units.analogy: Pronouncing German is like tuning a radio: most letters map to one predictable sound, so once you know the station frequencies (letter sounds) you can receive almost any word you read aloud.
units.breakage: this breaks with borrowed words (Job, Handy) and fixed letter teams (ei, sch, ch) that carry their own signal — those must be learned as whole chunks, not assembled letter by letter.

units.title: Numbers, Age, and Personal Details
units.scenario: You fill out a registration form at the Sprachschule.
units.can_do: I can count from zero, construct German numbers to 100, say my age and birthday, and share contact details.

foundations.title: Count from zero before using numbers
foundations.explanation: Learn the small sequence as sound and rhythm before using it in forms: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf, zwölf, dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn, sechzehn, siebzehn, achtzehn, neunzehn, zwanzig. Thirteen through nineteen mostly combine the small number with zehn, with shortened forms in sechzehn and siebzehn.
foundations.practice: Count 0–20 forward, 20–0 backward, and then count ten nearby objects without looking at the written list.

foundations.title: Build larger numbers from ones and tens
foundations.explanation: German says the ones before the tens for 21–99: 24 is vier-und-zwanzig, literally four-and-twenty. The tens anchors are zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig, sechzig, siebzig, achtzig, and neunzig. Numbers are written as one word, and eins normally becomes ein inside a compound such as einundzwanzig.
foundations.practice: Construct 21, 24, 37, 58, and 99 aloud from their ones and tens; then write each as one German word.

foundations.title: Choose the rule for the job
foundations.explanation: Age uses sein in German: Ich bin achtundzwanzig Jahre alt. Phone numbers are usually spoken as clear digits or short groups, while calendar dates use ordinal forms such as der dritte and am dritten März. The number stays the same idea, but its grammatical job changes its form.
foundations.practice: Say your age as one number, your phone number as grouped digits, and your birthday with am plus an ordinal date.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Null eins sieben sechs, fünf vier drei zwei eins null.

pronunciation: Stress digit groups when reading phone numbers.
units.pragmatics: Pause between digit groups; German mobiles often start with 015x or 017x.
units.culture: Dates use day.month.year; the first uses der erste.
units.speaking_prompt: Say your age, birthday, and phone number at a registration desk.
units.writing_prompt: Complete a form with name, age, address, email, and birthday.

checks.prompt: Welche Reihe zählt korrekt von null bis fünf?
choices: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf
null, ein, drei, zwei, vier, fünf
eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs
null, eins, zwei, vier, drei, fünf
checks.explanation: The basic sequence is null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf; fluent larger numbers depend on retrieving these anchors in order.

units.analogy: Building German numbers is like assembling toy bricks: 21 is one-and-twenty (einundzwanzig) — you say the units first, then the tens.
units.breakage: the analogy breaks for the teens (dreizehn, vierzehn), where the units come first but without und, and for the hundreds — so it is two or three assembly rules, not one universal one.

units.title: Family and Relationships
units.scenario: You show a photo of your family to a new friend in the course cafeteria.
units.can_do: I can describe my family members and ask simple questions about other people's families.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ja, das sind meine Eltern und mein Bruder.
dialogue.translation: Yes, my parents and my brother.

units.pragmatics: Family topics are common small talk; ask politely before personal questions.
units.culture: Familie remains central; many Germans visit parents regularly on Sundays.
units.speaking_prompt: Describe your family photo: who each person is and one detail about them.
units.writing_prompt: Write eight sentences about your family using haben and possessives.

checks.explanation: Siblings is a safe, common question.

units.analogy: Describing family is like labeling a family tree: possessive words (mein, dein) are name tags you attach to each branch.
units.breakage: the tree analogy breaks where grammar begins: the tag changes with the branch's gender and role (mein Bruder, meine Schwester, meinen Bruder), and German uses a different tag for his and her — a real tree has no gendered endings.

units.title: Daily Routines and Telling Time
units.scenario: You explain your typical weekday to a host family in Munich.
units.can_do: I can tell the time, describe daily routines, and use common time expressions.

vocabulary.example: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.

phrases.target: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.

dialogue.speaker: Gastmutter
dialogue.translation: When do you usually get up?

dialogue.speaker: Gastmutter
dialogue.translation: And when does your work start?

dialogue.speaker: Gastmutter
dialogue.translation: What do you do in the evening?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ich lerne Deutsch und gehe spazieren.
dialogue.translation: I study German and go for a walk.

pronunciation: In 'halb neun', halb means halfway to nine (= 8:30).
units.pragmatics: Punctuality is valued; say 'Gleich' or 'Ich komme in fünf Minuten' if late.
units.culture: Shops close early; many workers start around 8:00–9:00.
units.speaking_prompt: Describe your weekday from morning to evening with times.
units.writing_prompt: Write a schedule for Monday with at least six time expressions.

checks.explanation: Halb vier = half way to four = 3:30.

checks.prompt: Wo steht 'auf' in 'Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.'?
checks.explanation: Separable prefix goes to clause end.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Es ist viertel nach acht.' Wie spät?
Was passt: '___ Wochenende schlafe ich lange.'

units.analogy: Separable verbs are like a sandwich: the verb splits and the prefix travels to the very end of the sentence, holding the meaning together around the filling.
units.breakage: the sandwich breaks when the verb enters a subordinate clause or the infinitive with zu (aufzustehen), because the two halves snap back together — the split is a main-clause behavior, not a property of the verb.

units.title: Food, Drinks, and Ordering
units.scenario: You order lunch at a café near the Goethe-Institut.
units.can_do: I can read a simple menu, order food and drinks, and ask for the bill.

dialogue.speaker: Kellner
dialogue.translation: What would you like to drink?

pronunciation: 'ö' in 'möchten' is rounded, like 'er' with rounded lips.
units.pragmatics: Say bitte and danke; tipping ~5–10% by rounding up is common.
units.culture: Cash was traditionally preferred; card acceptance has grown since 2020.
units.speaking_prompt: Role-play ordering a drink, a dish, and asking for the bill.
units.writing_prompt: Write a short dialogue ordering lunch for two people.

checks.prompt: Was sagt man vor dem Essen?
Sie hören 'Sonst noch etwas?' Was meint der Kellner?

units.analogy: Ordering food is a call-and-response ritual: a fixed opener (Ich hätte gern ...), a fixed reply, a fixed closing — you learn the turns first, then swap in new items.
units.breakage: the ritual breaks the moment the reply is unexpected, because you then need the follow-up questions (Haben Sie ...?, Was kostet ...?) — the script is a skeleton, not the conversation.

units.title: At Home: Rooms and Furniture
units.scenario: A neighbor helps you describe your new apartment in Hamburg.
units.can_do: I can name rooms and furniture and say where things are in my home.
grammar: There is/are: es gibt / es ist

phrases.target: Der Tisch steht in der Küche.
phrases.translation: The table is in the kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Sie hat drei Zimmer und eine Küche.
dialogue.translation: It has three rooms and a kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.translation: In the bedroom, next to the window.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Sie ist okay, die Wohnung ist gemütlich.
dialogue.translation: It's okay, the apartment is cozy.

pronunciation: Umlaut ü in 'gemütlich' is like French 'u'.
units.pragmatics: Renting requires Anmeldung (registration) at the Bürgeramt within weeks of moving.
units.culture: Many cities have Mietpreisbremse (rent cap) rules; contracts are taken seriously.
units.speaking_prompt: Give a short tour of your home room by room.
units.writing_prompt: Describe your ideal apartment in eight sentences.

checks.explanation: German counts all rooms, not only bedrooms.
All can express location with dative.

units.analogy: Prepositions of place are like a floor plan: in, auf, neben plus the dative mark where things sit, a static map of the room.
units.breakage: the floor-plan analogy breaks the moment something moves: direction takes the accusative instead (in das Zimmer, an die Wand) — the same preposition has two map layers, and only the verb tells you which one to read.

units.title: Shopping: Clothes and Prices
units.scenario: You buy clothes at a department store in Frankfurt.
units.can_do: I can ask for sizes and prices, try items on, and pay at the checkout.

phrases.target: Haben Sie das in Größe M?
phrases.translation: Do you have that in size M?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.translation: Yes, I'm looking for a jacket.

pronunciation: Vowel length in 'Preis' vs. 'Preis' short in some dialects.
units.pragmatics: Say Guten Tag when entering; danke schön when leaving even without buying.
units.culture: Prices include MwSt (VAT); displayed prices are what you pay.
units.speaking_prompt: Ask for a item, size, price, and say you'll take it.
units.writing_prompt: Write an email asking if a shop has a product in your size.

checks.prompt: Was fragen Sie nach dem Preis?
Sie hören 'Größe L'. Was sucht die Person?

units.analogy: Polite shopping requests are like a vending machine: insert the exact request format (Ich möchte ..., bitte) and the goods come back.
units.breakage: the vending machine breaks because a real vendor asks questions back — size, color, count — so you need the size adjectives, plural forms, and price-reading phrases the machine never requests.

units.title: Hobbies and Free Time
units.scenario: You talk about weekend plans with classmates after lesson.
units.can_do: I can say what I like doing in my free time and make simple plans.

phrases.translation: Do you have time on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ich lese gern und spiele Klavier.
dialogue.translation: I like reading and play piano.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ja, im Sommer fast jeden Tag.

dialogue.speaker: Klassenkamerad
dialogue.translation: Do you have time on Sunday?

pronunciation: Stress first syllable in HO-bby, SPORt.
Rolling or light 'r' in 'Sport' varies by region.
units.pragmatics: Invitations often use du; confirm time and place clearly.
units.culture: Vereine (clubs) are popular for sports and music; many activities are organized.
units.speaking_prompt: Talk about three hobbies and invite someone to join one.
units.writing_prompt: Write a message inviting a friend to an activity this weekend.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Am Wochenende habe ich frei.' Was bedeutet das?
checks.explanation: frei haben = to have time off.
Leider geht es nicht is polite.

units.analogy: Modal verbs are the engine of the sentence: ich kann schwimmen puts the engine (kann) in second position and leaves the raw activity (schwimmen) as untouched fuel at the end.
units.breakage: the engine analogy breaks because modals are not interchangeable — möchten is a polite wish, not 'would like to be able' — each engine changes the meaning of the trip, and the fuel must never be conjugated.

units.title: Weather and Seasons
units.scenario: You discuss today's weather with colleagues before a lunch walk.
units.can_do: I can describe the weather, name seasons, and say what I wear accordingly.

dialogue.speaker: Kollegin
dialogue.target: Na, wie ist das Wetter draußen?
dialogue.translation: So, what's the weather like outside?

dialogue.speaker: Kollegin
dialogue.target: Schade! Gestern war es so schön.
dialogue.translation: Too bad! Yesterday was so nice.

dialogue.speaker: Kollegin
dialogue.target: Im Herbst wechselt das Wetter schnell.
dialogue.translation: In autumn the weather changes quickly.

pronunciation: ß after long vowels: heiß, groß.
units.pragmatics: Weather small talk is safe and common in elevators and shops.
units.culture: Germany has four distinct seasons; Layering is practical year-round.
units.speaking_prompt: Describe today's weather and what you are wearing.
units.writing_prompt: Write four sentences per season about typical weather and activities.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'minus fünf Grad'. Wie ist es?
Welche Jahreszeit kommt nach dem Sommer?

units.analogy: Talking about the weather is like reading snapshot cards: es regnet, es ist kalt — impersonal es plays the empty subject English needs as 'it'.
units.breakage: the snapshot breaks with seasons, because the frame is glued to the season (im Sommer, im Winter) — you learn the preposition and the season as one fixed chunk, not from the snapshot.

units.title: Getting Around: Directions and Transport
units.scenario: You ask for directions to the Goethe-Institut after exiting the U-Bahn.
units.can_do: I can understand simple directions, buy a ticket, and name means of transport.

phrases.translation: Thank you very much for the help!

dialogue.speaker: Passant
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, where is the Goethe-Institut?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Gehen Sie geradeaus und dann links.

dialogue.speaker: Passant
dialogue.target: Sie können auch die U-Bahn nehmen.
dialogue.translation: You can also take the subway.

pronunciation: The 'ü' in 'fünf' is rounded high front vowel.
Stress on first syllable: BAhnhof, HALtestelle.
units.pragmatics: Always say Entschuldigung before asking strangers; Sie for unknown adults.
units.culture: Public transit is reliable; validate tickets where required (Entwertung).
units.speaking_prompt: Ask for directions from a landmark to another; include transport option.
units.writing_prompt: Write directions from your hotel to the nearest train station.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Dann links.' Was machen Sie?
Was kaufen Sie an der Maschine?

units.analogy: Giving directions is like planning a delivery route: fixed landmarks plus turn commands (geradeaus, links, rechts) that move the listener step by step.
units.breakage: the route analogy breaks with polite commands (Gehen Sie ...) and with two-way prepositions (an der Ecke vs. um die Ecke) — the same corner changes case depending on whether you stand at it or move around it.

units.title: Health and the Doctor
units.scenario: You visit a Hausarzt because of a cold and need to explain symptoms.
units.can_do: I can describe simple health problems, understand basic medical advice, and make a doctor's appointment.

phrases.target: Seit wann haben Sie die Beschwerden?
phrases.translation: Since when have you had symptoms?

phrases.target: Nehmen Sie dieses Medikament dreimal täglich.
phrases.translation: Take this medicine three times daily.
I have a sore throat and cough.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.target: Ich habe seit zwei Tagen Husten und Fieber.
dialogue.translation: I've had cough and fever for two days.

dialogue.speaker: Arzt
dialogue.target: Nein, eine Erkältung. Ruhen Sie sich aus.
dialogue.translation: No, a cold. Get some rest.

pronunciation: The 'ch' in 'ich' when saying 'Ich fühle mich …'.
units.pragmatics: Address doctors with Sie; bring insurance card (Krankenversicherungskarte).
units.culture: Hausarzt is first contact; pharmacies advise on minor issues (Apotheke).
units.speaking_prompt: Describe symptoms to a doctor and ask one follow-up question.
units.writing_prompt: Write a sick note email to your employer explaining you cannot come today.

checks.explanation: Kopfschmerzen is plural; no article needed often, but die if used.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Gute Besserung!' Was wünscht man?
'Weil ich krank bin' – wo steht das Verb?
Wo holen Sie Medikament ohne Rezept?

units.analogy: Describing pain is like filing an error report: name the component (der Kopf) and the failure signal (tut weh).
units.breakage: the report analogy breaks when the conversation turns to advice and obligation — Sie müssen, Sie sollten — because now it is a negotiation about actions, not a description of symptoms.

units.title: Work and Professions
units.scenario: You discuss your job at a networking event for newcomers in Germany.
units.can_do: I can talk about my profession, workplace, and simple work routines.

phrases.translation: What do you do for work?

phrases.target: Ich arbeite von neun bis fünf.
phrases.translation: I work from nine to five.
How do you like the job?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Bei einer Firma in Hamburg, im Homeoffice.
dialogue.translation: At a company in Hamburg, remote.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ja, meine Kollegen sind sehr freundlich.
dialogue.translation: Yes, my colleagues are very friendly.

pronunciation: Profession nouns ending -er stress first syllable: LEhrer.
units.pragmatics: Job titles without article after sein; feminine forms increasingly used (-in).
units.culture: Work-life boundaries matter; punctuality and direct communication are valued.
units.speaking_prompt: Introduce your profession, employer, and typical workday.
units.writing_prompt: Write a short LinkedIn-style bio in German (6–8 sentences).

checks.prompt: 'Ich bin Lehrer.' – braucht man einen Artikel?
Sie lesen 'von 8 bis 16 Uhr'. Wann endet die Arbeit?

units.analogy: Job vocabulary is like an inventory of roles: each profession is a labeled shelf (der Arzt, die Ärztin).
units.breakage: the inventory breaks because German job language expects the feminine -in form in job ads and formal contexts, and because many job titles borrow from English — the shelves keep gaining new labels the old system never designed.

units.title: Talking About the Past
units.scenario: You share what you did last weekend with your tandem partner.
units.can_do: I can use Perfekt with haben/sein to describe past events and experiences.

phrases.target: Was hast du am Wochenende gemacht?
phrases.translation: What did you do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Partner
dialogue.target: Was hast du gestern Abend gemacht?
dialogue.translation: What did you do yesterday evening?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ich habe gekocht und einen Film gesehen.
dialogue.translation: I cooked and watched a film.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Einen deutschen Film. Er war interessant.
dialogue.translation: A German film. It was interesting.

dialogue.speaker: Partner
dialogue.target: Bist du schon mal nach Berlin gefahren?
dialogue.translation: Have you ever been to Berlin?

pronunciation: Past participle ge- stress: geKAUft, geGANGen.
Silent 'h' in gehabt in fast speech.
units.pragmatics: Past tense in speech is mostly Perfekt; Präteritum of sein/haben/modals is common.
units.culture: Sharing weekend activities is typical Monday small talk at work.
units.speaking_prompt: Narrate your last weekend using at least five Perfekt verbs.
units.writing_prompt: Write a diary entry about yesterday in 80–100 words.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Was hast du gemacht?' Welche Zeitform?

units.analogy: The Perfekt is like a photo album: every past event gets a caption built from an auxiliary (haben) and a frozen snapshot participle (gemacht).
units.breakage: the album analogy breaks with movement and change-of-state verbs, which take sein (ich bin gefahren), and the participle of separable verbs wraps the prefix around it (aufgestanden) — some pictures travel with a different carrier and some snapshots are re-sealed.

units.title: Travel, Hotels, and Tourism
units.scenario: You check into a hotel in Vienna during a short trip.
units.can_do: I can book accommodation, ask about hotel services, and handle travel problems.

phrases.target: Ich habe eine Reservierung auf den Namen …
phrases.translation: I have a reservation under the name …

dialogue.speaker: Rezeptionist
dialogue.translation: Good evening! Do you have a reservation?

dialogue.speaker: Gast
dialogue.target: Ja, auf den Namen Keller, für zwei Nächte.
dialogue.translation: Yes, under Keller, for two nights.

dialogue.speaker: Rezeptionist
dialogue.target: Könnten Sie bitte Ihren Ausweis zeigen?
dialogue.translation: Could you show your ID please?

dialogue.speaker: Rezeptionist
dialogue.target: Ja, das Passwort steht auf der Karte.
dialogue.translation: Yes, the password is on the card.

dialogue.speaker: Gast
dialogue.target: Vielen Dank. Bis wann ist Frühstück?
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Until when is breakfast?

pronunciation: French loanwords keep stress: Reservierung, Hotel.
units.pragmatics: Hotels require ID registration (Meldepflicht); checkout is often by 11:00.
units.culture: Austria and Germany share language but differ in some vocabulary (Jänner vs. Januar).
units.speaking_prompt: Role-play hotel check-in including a problem and solution.
units.writing_prompt: Write an email confirming a hotel booking with dates and special requests.

checks.prompt: Was zeigen Sie an der Rezeption?
Sie lesen 'Frühstück 7–10 Uhr'. Wann beginnt es?
Sie hören 'Die Klimaanlage funktioniert nicht.' Was ist das Problem?

units.analogy: Travel talk is like a railway of scripted stations: check-in phrases, booking questions, and schedule words are stops you arrive at in order.
units.breakage: the station model breaks when plans change and you must re-route — weil- and wenn-clauses push the verb to the end, so the re-routing itself changes the word order of every station.

units.title: Phone Calls and Messages
units.scenario: You call a language school to ask about course times and leave a message.
units.can_do: I can make and answer simple phone calls, leave messages, and understand voicemail.

phrases.target: Kann ich bitte mit Herrn Schmidt sprechen?
phrases.translation: May I speak with Mr. Schmidt?
He is not here right now.

phrases.target: Ich rufe später noch einmal an.

dialogue.speaker: Anrufer
dialogue.target: Guten Tag, hier spricht Jonas. Ich interessiere mich für einen A2-Kurs.
dialogue.translation: Good day, Jonas speaking. I'm interested in an A2 course.

dialogue.speaker: Anrufer
dialogue.target: Danke. Könnten Sie mir die Zeiten nennen?
dialogue.translation: Thanks. Could you tell me the times?

dialogue.speaker: Empfang
dialogue.target: Der Kurs beginnt am 3. April, montags und mittwochs.
dialogue.translation: The course starts April 3, Mon and Wed.

pronunciation: Clear enunciation critical on phone; spell names if unclear.
units.pragmatics: State name and purpose immediately; Sie on business calls.
units.culture: Germans often identify company when answering; expect directness.
units.speaking_prompt: Leave a voicemail requesting course information and a callback number.
units.writing_prompt: Write an SMS rescheduling a meeting to tomorrow at 3 p.m.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Die Leitung ist besetzt.' Was tun Sie?
Was ist höflich bei schnellem Sprechen?

units.analogy: Phone formulas are like a compressed radio protocol: fixed openers (Hier ist ...), short confirmations, and a predictable sign-off.
units.breakage: the protocol breaks on a bad connection — you must ask for repetition (Wie bitte? Können Sie das wiederholen?) and spell names with the alphabet, moves the script never contains.

units.title: Invitations and Making Plans
units.scenario: You invite colleagues to a birthday dinner and negotiate the details.
units.can_do: I can invite others, accept or decline, and agree on time and place.
grammar: Accusative time: am Samstag um 19 Uhr

phrases.target: Hättest du Lust, am Freitag essen zu gehen?
phrases.translation: Fancy going out to eat on Friday?

phrases.target: Treffen wir uns vor dem Restaurant.
phrases.translation: Let's meet in front of the restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: Einladende
dialogue.target: Ich mache am Samstag eine Party. Kommst du?
dialogue.translation: I'm having a party Saturday. Coming?

dialogue.speaker: Einladende
dialogue.target: Nur dich! Aber du kannst Getränke mitbringen.
dialogue.translation: Just you! But you can bring drinks.

dialogue.speaker: Freund
dialogue.translation: Great, I'm looking forward to it!

units.pragmatics: Confirm time, address, and whether to bring something; punctuality expected.
units.culture: Birthdays: Germans may host 'Einladung' where host provides food; ask what's needed.
units.speaking_prompt: Invite someone to an event and negotiate date, time, and location.
units.writing_prompt: Write a short invitation message including RSVP request.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Soll ich etwas mitbringen?' Was will die Person wissen?

units.analogy: Making plans is like negotiating a shared calendar: the invitation is a move (Kannst du ...?), the acceptance or decline is the answering move.
units.breakage: the calendar analogy breaks because a polite decline carries a reason, usually a weil-clause with verb-last order — the calendar records the answer, the grammar rebuilds the sentence to give it.

units.title: Describing People and Appearance
units.scenario: You help police describe a lost contact person at a festival (language practice scenario).
units.can_do: I can describe people's appearance and personality using simple adjectives.

phrases.target: Er trägt heute einen blauen Pullover.
phrases.translation: He's wearing a blue sweater today.

dialogue.speaker: Person A
dialogue.target: Entschuldigung, haben Sie meinen Freund gesehen?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, have you seen my friend?

dialogue.speaker: Person A
dialogue.target: Er ist mittelgroß, mit Bart und Brille.

dialogue.speaker: Person B
dialogue.target: Ja, ich habe ihn vorhin gesehen.

pronunciation: Adjective stress before noun: GRÜne Jacke.
units.pragmatics: Descriptions start general → specific; height in meters in Germany.
units.culture: Privacy norms are strong; only describe strangers in appropriate contexts.
units.speaking_prompt: Describe a friend or celebrity with five appearance and two personality traits.
units.writing_prompt: Write a 'person gone missing' notice for a classroom exercise.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Er trägt eine Brille.' Was hat er?

units.analogy: Describing a person is like painting a portrait in layers: size and hair first, then character traits.
units.breakage: the portrait breaks with comparison and judgment — größer als, so alt wie, ich finde ihn nett — because comparing needs als/wie and judging needs verbs of opinion the paintbrush model does not provide.

units.title: Media and Entertainment
units.scenario: You discuss films, series, and music with friends after a Goethe film night.
units.can_do: I can talk about media preferences, give simple recommendations, and understand program listings.

phrases.target: Ich finde die Serie sehr gut.
phrases.translation: I find the series very good.

dialogue.speaker: Freund
dialogue.target: Hast du den Film gestern gesehen?
dialogue.translation: Did you see the film yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Freund
dialogue.translation: Do you also like German series?

units.pragmatics: Use du with friends; opinions are stated directly but can be softened with finde.
units.culture: Public broadcasters ARD/ZDF are central; streaming is widely used.
units.speaking_prompt: Recommend a film or series and explain why in three reasons.
units.writing_prompt: Write a short review of a film you saw recently.

checks.prompt: 'Ich finde den Film gut.' – welcher Fall nach finde?
Sie lesen '20:15 Uhr'. Wann beginnt der Film?
Sie hören 'Kannst du etwas empfehlen?' Was will die Person?

units.analogy: Media talk is like a TV guide: genres and schedules listed factually (der Film läuft um acht).
units.breakage: the guide analogy breaks the moment you give an opinion: mir gefällt ..., ich mag ... flip the sentence so the liked thing, not the liker, is the subject — a guide lists, opinions judge.

units.title: Environment and City Life
units.scenario: You join a neighborhood cleanup and discuss recycling rules in your city.
units.can_do: I can talk about city facilities, simple environmental actions, and local services.

phrases.translation: Where is the nearest recycling center?

phrases.target: Ich fahre oft mit dem Fahrrad.
In unserer Stadt gibt es viele Parks.

dialogue.speaker: Nachbar
dialogue.target: Wissen Sie, wo die Glascontainer sind?
dialogue.translation: Do you know where the glass containers are?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.translation: Yes, on the corner of Hauptstraße.

dialogue.speaker: Nachbar
dialogue.translation: Do you have to sort the bottles?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ja, nach Farbe: weiß, grün, braun.
dialogue.translation: Yes, by color: white, green, brown.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Stimmt. Ich fahre auch weniger Auto.

units.pragmatics: Pfand system: return bottles for deposit; strict waste sorting varies by Bundesland.
units.culture: German cities prioritize recycling; Feiertage affect collection schedules.
units.speaking_prompt: Explain how waste is sorted in your city and give two eco tips.
units.writing_prompt: Write a poster text encouraging neighbors to recycle correctly.

checks.prompt: Sie lesen 'Bitte nicht wegwerfen!' Was soll man nicht tun?

units.analogy: City life is like a services system: the S-Bahn runs, the market opens — often described with the impersonal man (man kann ...).
units.breakage: the system analogy breaks because man erases the actor: 'man nimmt die U-Bahn' names no one, and the passive-like reports hide the agent too — the city runs itself in this grammar.

units.title: Festivals and Traditions
units.scenario: You celebrate Oktoberfest season and explain German holidays to international friends.
units.can_do: I can describe common festivals, traditions, and holiday customs in German-speaking countries.

phrases.target: Wie feiert man Weihnachten in Deutschland?
phrases.translation: How is Christmas celebrated in Germany?
What do you do on New Year's Eve?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ja, in München. Viele Besucher aus aller Welt.
dialogue.translation: Yes, in Munich. Many visitors worldwide.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.translation: Pretzels, chicken, and of course beer.

dialogue.speaker: Freund
dialogue.translation: And how do you celebrate New Year's Eve?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Mit Freunden, Feuerwerk und 'Dinner for One'.
dialogue.translation: With friends, fireworks, and 'Dinner for One'.

units.pragmatics: Holiday greetings are expected; regional differences are a conversation topic.
units.culture: Christmas Eve (24 Dec) is main family day; 'Dinner for One' airs on Silvester.
units.speaking_prompt: Explain one German holiday tradition to someone unfamiliar with it.
units.writing_prompt: Write a postcard message about a festival you attended.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Morgen ist Feiertag.' Was bedeutet das?

units.analogy: Traditions are like a recurring ritual calendar: fixed seasons and fixed activities in fixed phrases (Weihnachten feiern, Ostereier suchen).
units.breakage: the ritual model breaks with regional variants — Karneval, Fasching, Fastnacht — and with wish phrases (Ich würde gern ...), where the subjunctive marks the wish as not-yet-real, something no calendar records.

units.title: Education and Career Planning
units.scenario: You consult a Berufsberater about vocational training vs. university in Germany.
units.can_do: I can discuss education paths, qualifications, and career goals with some detail.

vocabulary.example: Ich bewerbe mich um die Stelle.

phrases.translation: I want to further my education.

phrases.target: Ich habe gehört, dass die Nachfrage hoch ist.
phrases.translation: I heard that demand is high.

phrases.target: Könnten Sie mir den Unterschied erklären?
Nach dem Abschluss suche ich eine Stelle.
phrases.translation: After graduating I'll look for a job.

phrases.target: Das duale System kombiniert Theorie und Praxis.
phrases.translation: Dual system combines theory and practice.

dialogue.speaker: Berater
dialogue.target: Interessieren Sie sich für Studium oder Ausbildung?
dialogue.translation: Are you interested in university or vocational training?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ich denke an eine Ausbildung, weil ich praktisch lernen möchte.
dialogue.translation: I'm considering training because I want practical learning.

dialogue.speaker: Berater
dialogue.translation: Do you already have a CV?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ja, aber ich muss ihn noch anpassen.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I still need to adapt it.

units.pragmatics: Formal Sie in counseling; bring documents organized.
units.culture: Dual Ausbildung is prestigious; university paths vary by Bundesland fees/history.
units.speaking_prompt: Explain your education background and five-year career goal.
units.writing_prompt: Write a paragraph for a cover letter stating motivation and qualifications.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Bewerben Sie sich frühzeitig.' Was raten sie?

units.analogy: Career planning is like a branching roadmap: Ausbildung, Studium, and Weiterbildung are forks that open different routes.
units.breakage: the roadmap breaks with time and condition — seit drei Jahren studiere ich, wenn ich fertig bin — because routes change with duration and condition, and the verb order changes with them.

units.title: Expressing Opinions and Discussing
units.scenario: You debate remote work policies in a B1 discussion circle.
units.can_do: I can express and justify opinions, agree, disagree, and ask for clarification.

phrases.target: Meiner Meinung nach ist das sinnvoll.
Einerseits spart man Zeit, andererseits fehlt der Kontakt.
phrases.translation: On one hand you save time, on the other contact is missing.

dialogue.speaker: Moderator
dialogue.target: Soll Homeoffice Pflicht oder Option sein?
dialogue.translation: Should remote work be mandatory or optional?

dialogue.speaker: Teilnehmer A
dialogue.target: Meiner Meinung nach sollte es eine Option bleiben.
dialogue.translation: In my view it should remain optional.

dialogue.speaker: Teilnehmer B
dialogue.target: Da stimme ich zu, aber nicht für alle Berufe.
dialogue.translation: I agree, but not for all professions.

dialogue.speaker: Moderator
dialogue.target: Guter Punkt. Wer sieht das anders?
dialogue.translation: Good point. Who sees it differently?

pronunciation: obwohl: verb goes to end in clause.
units.pragmatics: Use softeners: vielleicht, teilweise; avoid shouting down others.
units.culture: Consensus-seeking is valued but direct debate is acceptable in educated settings.
units.speaking_prompt: State opinion on a current topic with two reasons and one counterargument.
units.writing_prompt: Write a forum post agreeing partly and adding your own view.

checks.prompt: 'Obwohl es regnet, gehe ich raus.' – Verb in Nebensatz?
Sie hören 'Da stimme ich zu.' Was drückt die Person aus?

units.analogy: An opinion is like a two-sided coin: the claim on one side, the justification on the other (Ich finde, dass ..., weil ...).
units.breakage: the coin breaks because dass forces verb-last order and ich glaube shifts the claim into a subordinate shape — the sentence architecture changes with the verb of saying, not just the content.

units.title: News and Current Events
units.scenario: You summarize a short news article for your German conversation class.
units.can_do: I can understand main points of news reports and summarize events and consequences.
grammar: Passive in news: wurde + Part. II

phrases.target: Laut Berichten wurde das Gesetz verabschiedet.
phrases.translation: According to reports the law was passed.

dialogue.speaker: Lehrer
dialogue.target: Und welche Auswirkungen könnte das haben?
dialogue.translation: And what effects could that have?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Mehr Jobs in der Solarbranche, denke ich.
dialogue.translation: More jobs in solar, I think.

units.pragmatics: News German uses passive and nominal style; stick to facts when summarizing.
units.culture: Public media Tagesschau is a reference; regional papers vary politically.
units.speaking_prompt: Summarize a news article in five sentences: who, what, when, why, impact.
units.writing_prompt: Write a short news-style paragraph about a local event.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Die Folgen sind unklar.' Was meint der Sprecher?

units.analogy: News is like an evidence chain: source, event, consequence — often reported in the passive (wurde gemeldet).
units.breakage: the chain analogy breaks because the passive removes the actor: 'es wurde beschlossen' does not say who decided — news omits the very link the chain model insists on.

units.title: Health, Lifestyle, and Prevention
units.scenario: You discuss stress management and healthy habits with a coach at work.
units.can_do: I can discuss health risks, lifestyle choices, and give advice using modal and conditional forms.

phrases.target: Versuchen Sie, früher ins Bett zu gehen.
phrases.translation: Try to go to bed earlier.

dialogue.speaker: Coach
dialogue.target: Planen Sie feste Pausen und Bewegung ein.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Das klingt machbar. Ich fange morgen an.
dialogue.translation: That sounds doable. I'll start tomorrow.

units.pragmatics: Health advice uses Sie in professional settings; privacy around illness is strong.
units.culture: Betriebliche Gesundheitsförderung is common; Hausarzt gatekeeps specialist care.
units.speaking_prompt: Discuss your lifestyle and propose three concrete improvements.
units.writing_prompt: Write advice email to a friend who is overworking.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Machen Sie regelmäßig Pausen.' Was empfiehlt man?

units.analogy: Prevention is like a balance sheet: habit on one side, consequence on the other (wenn ich ..., dann ...).
units.breakage: the balance-sheet analogy breaks with purpose constructions — um ... zu — because purpose is a direction, not a balance, and it needs the infinitive clause the ledger never uses.

units.title: Culture, Art, and Museums
units.scenario: You visit a museum and discuss an exhibition with a guide and classmates.
units.can_do: I can describe artworks, express aesthetic reactions, and understand cultural program information.

phrases.target: Was hat Ihnen am besten gefallen?
Das Werk, das wir gesehen haben, war provokativ.
phrases.translation: The work we saw was provocative.

phrases.target: Der Künstler, dessen Bilder hier hängen, ist bekannt.
phrases.translation: The artist whose pictures hang here is famous.

phrases.target: Ich finde die Farben sehr intensiv.
phrases.translation: I find the colors very intense.

phrases.target: Gibt es eine Führung auf Englisch?
phrases.translation: Is there a tour in English?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.target: Willkommen zur Führung durch die moderne Abteilung.
dialogue.translation: Welcome to the modern section tour.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.translation: Which painting is the most famous?

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.target: Das Bild dort, das Sie meinen, ist von Beckmann.
dialogue.translation: The picture there you mean is by Beckmann.

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.target: Ja, es entstand nach dem Krieg.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it was created after the war.

units.pragmatics: Museum etiquette: quiet voice; ask before photos.
units.culture: Kulturpass and free days vary; many museums offer reduced student tickets.
units.speaking_prompt: Describe a work of art and interpret its mood and message.
units.writing_prompt: Write a short exhibition review for a blog.

checks.prompt: Sie lesen 'Fotografieren verboten.' Was dürfen Sie nicht?
Sie hören 'Willkommen zur Führung.' Wo sind Sie?

units.analogy: Art history is like a guided museum tour: eras, artists, and works described in order.
units.breakage: the tour analogy breaks with the written/spoken past split — Präteritum for the guidebook, Perfekt for the guided conversation — the same tour is told in two different tenses depending on the medium.

units.title: Technology and Digital Life
units.scenario: You troubleshoot online bureaucracy and discuss digital privacy with a neighbor.
units.can_do: I can discuss technology use, online services, and digital security in everyday contexts.

phrases.translation: You need to update the software.

phrases.target: Um das Formular zu senden, brauchen Sie eine Signatur.
phrases.translation: To send the form you need a signature.

phrases.target: Können Sie mir Schritt für Schritt helfen?
phrases.translation: Can you help me step by step?

dialogue.speaker: Nachbar
dialogue.target: Haben Sie Probleme mit dem Elster-Portal?

dialogue.speaker: Nachbar
dialogue.target: Ja, um Ihre Daten zu schützen.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Danke, ich mache das heute Abend.

pronunciation: Compound stress often on first element: PASSwort.
units.pragmatics: Digital bureaucracy (Behörden) expects correct formats; keep copies of submissions.
units.culture: GDPR (DSGVO) shapes privacy language; Germans may be cautious with data sharing.
units.speaking_prompt: Explain a tech problem and the steps you took to solve it.
units.writing_prompt: Write instructions for a colleague on enabling 2FA on an email account.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Bitte aktualisieren Sie die App.' Was soll man tun?

units.analogy: Digital life is like a device manual: verbs of use and clear steps (herunterladen, einloggen).
units.breakage: the manual breaks with time ordering — bevor, nachdem — because sequencing clauses reorder the verbs, and with the fact that most tech vocabulary is borrowed English that ignores German spelling rules.

units.title: Relationships and Communication
units.scenario: You mediate a misunderstanding between flatmates about shared responsibilities.
units.can_do: I can discuss relationships, express feelings, and negotiate compromises clearly.
grammar: Subjunctive II for soft requests: könntest du

phrases.target: Ich schlage vor, dass wir einen Putzplan machen.
phrases.translation: I suggest we make a cleaning rota.

dialogue.speaker: Mitbewohner A
dialogue.target: Ich bin sauer, die Küche ist immer schmutzig.
dialogue.translation: I'm angry, the kitchen is always dirty.

dialogue.speaker: Mitbewohner B
dialogue.target: Sorry, ich habe es nicht gemerkt.

dialogue.speaker: Mitbewohner A
dialogue.translation: Could you please wash up more often?

dialogue.speaker: Mitbewohner B
dialogue.target: Ja, wenn du den Müll rausbringst.
dialogue.translation: Yes, if you take out the trash.

dialogue.speaker: Mitbewohner A
dialogue.translation: Deal. Shall we make a plan?

dialogue.speaker: Mitbewohner B
dialogue.target: Gute Idee, dann gibt es keine Streitereien.

units.pragmatics: Use ich-messages to reduce blame; du among flatmates is normal.
units.culture: WG (shared flat) culture is common for students; written rules help.
units.speaking_prompt: Role-play resolving a conflict using ich-statements and a compromise.
units.writing_prompt: Write a WG agreement paragraph on shared duties.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Findest du das fair?' Was will die Person?

units.analogy: Communication is like a bridge between two positions: feelings and reactions travel across it.
units.breakage: the bridge analogy breaks with polite subjunctives — Könntest du ...?, Ich hätte eine Frage — because requests bend reality toward possibility, and a bridge only carries what already exists.

units.title: Formal Writing and Complaints
units.scenario: You write a formal Beschwerde about a defective product to customer service.
units.can_do: I can write structured formal letters/emails with register, complaints, and requests for remedy.

phrases.target: Ich bitte Sie um eine Stellungnahme.
phrases.translation: I request a statement from you.

dialogue.speaker: Kunde
dialogue.target: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, am 5.3. kaufte ich einen Mixer.
dialogue.translation: Dear Sirs, on 5/3 I bought a mixer.

dialogue.speaker: Kunde
dialogue.target: Leider ist das Gerät nach zwei Wochen defekt.
dialogue.translation: Unfortunately the device broke after two weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Kunde
dialogue.target: Ich bitte um Austausch oder Erstattung.

dialogue.speaker: Service
dialogue.target: Bitte senden Sie uns die Rechnung.

dialogue.speaker: Kunde
dialogue.target: Beiliegend die Kopie. Mit freundlichen Grüßen …

pronunciation: Formal: clear articulation in phone follow-ups.
units.pragmatics: Formal Sie throughout; include date, product, proof; cite Gewährleistung if needed.
units.culture: Consumer rights strong in EU/Germany; written trail matters.
units.speaking_prompt: Draft oral summary of your complaint before writing.
units.writing_prompt: Write a full Beschwerde email with subject line, body, closing.

checks.prompt: Sie lesen 'beiliegend'. Was hat der Absender gemacht?
'Ich bitte um Erstattung.' – was will der Kunde?

units.analogy: A complaint letter is like a fixed skeleton: salutation, description, demand, closing — fill the bones with your case.
units.breakage: the skeleton breaks with fixed register words (hiermit, beigefügt, wir fordern Sie auf) that have no everyday equivalent — you cannot assemble them from conversational blocks, they must be learned as units.

units.title: Subjunctive and Hypotheticals
units.scenario: You discuss 'what if' scenarios about moving to another Bundesland.
units.can_do: I can use Konjunktiv II to express wishes, hypotheticals, and polite alternatives.

phrases.target: Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich reisen.
phrases.translation: If I were rich, I would travel.

phrases.target: Ich wünschte, ich könnte besser Deutsch.
phrases.translation: I wish I could speak German better.

dialogue.speaker: Freund
dialogue.target: Wenn du nach Berlin ziehen würdest, was würdest du vermissen?
dialogue.translation: If you moved to Berlin, what would you miss?

dialogue.speaker: Freund
dialogue.target: Wäre die Miete nicht zu hoch?
dialogue.translation: Wouldn't the rent be too high?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Ja, aber ich hätte mehr Jobchancen.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I'd have more job chances.

dialogue.speaker: Freund
dialogue.target: An deiner Stelle würde ich erst sparen.
dialogue.translation: In your place I'd save first.

units.pragmatics: Konjunktiv II softens requests; common in advice and unreal conditions.
units.culture: Regional hypotheticals touch Miete, Dialekt, and job markets.
units.speaking_prompt: Discuss three things you would do if you won time/money.
units.writing_prompt: Write five wenn-sentences about lifestyle changes.

checks.prompt: 'An Ihrer Stelle würde ich …' drückt … aus

units.analogy: The Konjunktiv II is like a parallel universe: wenn ich reich wäre marks a world that is not real.
units.breakage: the parallel-universe model breaks because polite requests use the same forms (Ich hätte gern, Könnten Sie ...) — the unreal marker also does everyday softness, so only context decides which universe you are in.

units.title: Job Applications and Interviews
units.scenario: You prepare for a Vorstellungsgespräch at a German Mittelstand company.
units.can_do: I can handle interview questions, present strengths, and ask relevant questions professionally.

phrases.target: Warum möchten Sie bei uns arbeiten?
phrases.translation: Why do you want to work with us?
Do you have questions for us?

phrases.target: Ich freue mich auf Ihre Rückmeldung.
phrases.translation: I look forward to your reply.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.target: Warum bewerben Sie sich auf diese Stelle?
dialogue.translation: Why are you applying for this position?

dialogue.speaker: Kandidat
dialogue.target: Weil ich Erfahrung im Projektmgmt habe und Ihr Unternehmen innovativ ist.
dialogue.translation: Because I have PM experience and your firm is innovative.

dialogue.speaker: Interviewer
dialogue.target: Wo sehen Sie sich in fünf Jahren?
dialogue.translation: Where do you see yourself in five years?

dialogue.speaker: Kandidat
dialogue.target: In einer verantwortungsvollen Rolle mit mehr Kundenkontakt.
dialogue.translation: In a responsible role with more client contact.

dialogue.speaker: Kandidat
dialogue.target: Ja, wie sieht die Einarbeitung aus?
dialogue.translation: Yes, what does onboarding look like?

units.pragmatics: Formal Sie, firm handshake, eye contact; prepare 2–3 questions for employer.
units.culture: Gehaltsfrage timing varies; research Brutto/Netto and local bands.
units.speaking_prompt: Practice a 90-second self-presentation for an interview.
units.writing_prompt: Write follow-up thank-you email after an interview.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Haben Sie Fragen an uns?' Was sollen Sie tun?
'Ich freue mich auf Ihre Rückmeldung.' steht …

units.analogy: An interview is like a two-sided match: your qualifications are evidence, the questions are probes.
units.breakage: the match analogy breaks with the formal Sie register and indirect questions (ob, wann) that invert word order — the grammar of caution changes the shape of every probe and answer.

units.title: Politics and Society
units.scenario: You join a Stammtisch debate on voting participation and civic duty.
units.can_do: I can understand and contribute to discussions on political topics with nuanced arguments.

phrases.target: Meines Erachtens sollte jeder wählen gehen.
phrases.translation: In my view everyone should vote.

dialogue.speaker: Teilnehmer
dialogue.target: Sinkt die Wahlbeteiligung, weil junge Wähler desinteressiert sind?
dialogue.translation: Is turnout falling because young voters are disinterested?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Nicht nur deshalb; auch strukturelle Hürden spielen eine Rolle.
dialogue.translation: Not only that; structural barriers also play a role.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Wahltermine, Informationszugang und Vertrauen in Politik.
dialogue.translation: Election dates, access to information, trust in politics.

dialogue.speaker: Teilnehmer
dialogue.target: Demokratie lebt vom Diskurs, nicht nur vom Kreuz.
dialogue.translation: Democracy lives on discourse, not just the ballot.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Da stimme ich voll und ganz zu.

units.pragmatics: Avoid aggressive confrontation; cite sources in formal debate.
units.culture: 16+ EU citizen local voting in some municipalities; Bundesländer differ.
units.speaking_prompt: Argue for or against compulsory voting with three points.
units.writing_prompt: Write an opinion piece paragraph on civic engagement.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Das Thema ist brisant.' Was bedeutet das?

units.analogy: Politics is like a system of institutions where processes happen — largely in the passive (wird beschlossen).
units.breakage: the system analogy breaks with Konjunktiv I in reported speech: 'die Regierung habe ...' carries 'allegedly' inside the verb — systems state facts, reports carry doubt in the same grammar.

units.title: Economics and Consumer Rights
units.scenario: You analyze a Verbraucherzentrale leaflet about subscription traps.
units.can_do: I can discuss economic trends, contracts, and consumer protection with precise vocabulary.

phrases.translation: Consumers have a right of withdrawal.
One should read the fine print.

phrases.target: Ich werde den Vertrag fristgerecht kündigen.
phrases.translation: I will cancel the contract in time.

dialogue.speaker: Berater
dialogue.target: Haben Sie den Vertrag online abgeschlossen?
dialogue.translation: Did you sign the contract online?

dialogue.speaker: Kunde
dialogue.target: Ja, und jetzt ziehen sie unerwartet ab.
dialogue.translation: Yes, and now they charge unexpectedly.

dialogue.speaker: Berater
dialogue.target: Prüfen Sie die Kündigungsfrist und Widerruf.

dialogue.speaker: Kunde
dialogue.target: Die Frist ist angeblich schon vorbei.
dialogue.translation: The period is allegedly already over.

dialogue.speaker: Berater
dialogue.target: Wir prüfen, ob die Klauseln wirksam sind.
dialogue.translation: We'll check if the clauses are valid.

units.pragmatics: Written cancellation often required; keep copies and dates.
units.culture: Verbraucherzentrale offers free/low-cost advice; EU Widerruf 14 days online.
units.speaking_prompt: Explain a subscription problem and legal steps you'd take.
units.writing_prompt: Write a Kündigung letter for a gym membership.

checks.prompt: 'Die Kosten belaufen sich auf 50 Euro.' – Präposition?
Sie lesen 'Kündigungsfrist: 4 Wochen.' Was ist wichtig?

units.analogy: Consumer rights are like a contract: right, duty, and remedy listed as clauses.
units.breakage: the contract analogy breaks with nominal style — das Rückgaberecht, die Widerrufsfrist — because official German packs whole verb meanings into compound nouns, and the contract becomes a list of packed boxes, not clauses.

units.title: Science and Research
units.scenario: You present a simplified research summary at a public Wissenschaftsforum.
units.can_do: I can understand academic summaries, explain methods, and discuss findings cautiously.

phrases.target: Die Daten deuten darauf hin, dass …
Es handelt sich um eine Langzeitstudie.

phrases.translation: Possibly there is a correlation effect.

dialogue.speaker: Moderator
dialogue.target: Was ist das Hauptergebnis Ihrer Studie?
dialogue.translation: What is the main result of your study?

dialogue.speaker: Forscher
dialogue.target: Wir haben einen Zusammenhang zwischen Schlaf und Konzentration festgestellt.
dialogue.translation: We found a link between sleep and concentration.

dialogue.speaker: Forscher
dialogue.target: Ja, statistisch signifikant, aber nicht kausal bewiesen.
dialogue.translation: Yes, statistically significant, but not causally proven.

units.pragmatics: Academic register avoids overclaiming; distinguish Korrelation vs. Kausalität.
units.culture: Public science communication (Wissenschaft im Dialog) is funded nationally.
units.speaking_prompt: Present a study summary with method, finding, and limitation.
units.writing_prompt: Write an abstract-style paragraph (80 words) on a topic you know.

checks.prompt: 'Die Daten deuten darauf hin' drückt … aus
Sie hören 'Weitere Forschung ist erforderlich.' Was meint der Sprecher?

units.analogy: Research is like a hypothesis loop: claim, evidence, and a hedge (soll, könnte).
units.breakage: the loop analogy breaks with nominalizations and the passive — die Untersuchung wurde durchgeführt — because scientific German removes the experimenter from the sentence, and the loop has no actor left.

units.title: Literature and Philosophy
units.scenario: You discuss a Kafka short story in an advanced Lesekreis.
units.can_do: I can interpret literary texts, discuss themes, and use abstract analytical language.

phrases.target: Die Ironie trifft die Leser unvorbereitet.

dialogue.speaker: Leiter
dialogue.target: Was fällt Ihnen an der Sprache auf?
dialogue.translation: What do you notice about the language?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Die Sätze sind lang und verschachtelt.
dialogue.translation: The sentences are long and nested.

dialogue.speaker: Leiter
dialogue.translation: Do you see parallels to the present?

units.pragmatics: Literary discussion uses Sie in formal circles; cite Textstellen.
units.culture: German literary canon includes Goethe, Kafka, Brecht; public readings common.
units.speaking_prompt: Give a 2-minute interpretation of a story theme.
units.writing_prompt: Write a Lesekreise contribution analyzing one metaphor.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Die Ironie trifft unvorbereitet.' Wirkung?

units.analogy: A literary text is like layers: plot on top, style below, interpretation deeper still.
units.breakage: the layer analogy breaks with interpretation grammar — würde bedeuten, könnte zeigen — because readings are proposals in the subjunctive, and layers of a fixed structure cannot be proposals.

units.title: Advanced Grammar Nuances
units.scenario: You refine error patterns in a C1 prep workshop focusing on B2 mastery.
units.can_do: I can control complex syntax: word order, case government, and register-appropriate structures.

phrases.target: Weil er müde war, ging er früh schlafen.
phrases.translation: Because he was tired, he went to bed early.

phrases.target: Er behauptet, das gemacht zu haben.
phrases.translation: He claims to have done that.

phrases.target: Wegen des Sturms fiel der Strom aus.
phrases.translation: Due to the storm the power went out.

dialogue.speaker: Trainer
dialogue.target: Finden Sie den Fehler: 'Ich habe gestern gegessen Pizza.'
dialogue.translation: Find the error: 'I have yesterday eaten pizza.'

dialogue.speaker: Trainer
dialogue.target: Sehr gut. Noch ein Satz mit doppelten Infinitiv?
dialogue.translation: Very good. Another with double infinitive?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Sie will das Problem gelöst haben.
dialogue.translation: She wants to have solved the problem.

pronunciation: Satzklammer: bracket intonation in long sentences.
units.pragmatics: Written German prefers genitive after wegen/trotz in formal register.
units.culture: Reform spelling (Rechtschreibreform) affects ß/ss rules.
units.speaking_prompt: Correct five deliberately flawed sentences orally.
units.writing_prompt: Rewrite a paragraph upgrading informal structures to formal B2.

checks.explanation: The more X, the more Y.

checks.prompt: Sie hören Korrektur von Genitiv. Welches Wort?

units.analogy: Grammar is like a machine with fine controls: particles (doch, ja, denn) are the knobs that tune a sentence's tone.
units.breakage: the machine analogy breaks because particles are context-dependent tones, not functions — the same knob means surprise, confirmation, or impatience depending on intonation, which no machine spec captures.

units.title: Professional Communication
units.scenario: You lead a hybrid team meeting presenting quarterly results.
units.can_do: I can chair meetings, report data, and negotiate next steps in professional German.

phrases.target: Laut Bericht sind wir im Plan.
phrases.translation: According to the report we are on track.

phrases.target: Ich sende das Protokoll heute Nachmittag.
phrases.translation: I'll send the minutes this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Leitung
dialogue.target: Der Umsatz ist um fünf Prozent gestiegen.

dialogue.speaker: Kollege
dialogue.target: Gibt es Risiken im nächsten Quartal?

dialogue.speaker: Leitung
dialogue.target: Guter Vorschlag. Wir stimmen das nächste Mal ab.
dialogue.translation: Good suggestion. We'll decide next time.

units.pragmatics: Meetings start on time; Protokoll documents Beschlüsse.
units.culture: Du in startups, Sie in traditional firms; hybrid etiquette evolving.
units.speaking_prompt: Lead a 3-minute meeting segment with agenda and action items.
units.writing_prompt: Write meeting minutes summarizing three decisions.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Wir vertagen Punkt vier.' Was passiert?

units.analogy: A meeting is like a structured exchange: agenda, decision, minutes — each with its fixed phrase.
units.breakage: the structure analogy breaks with hedging and indirectness — wäre es möglich, dürfte ich bitten — because professional German softens imperatives into questions, and the structure model has no slot for a question that means 'do it'.

units.title: Media Literacy and Criticism
units.scenario: You evaluate online sources for a seminar on Desinformation.
units.can_do: I can critique media messages, identify bias, and argue for source verification.

phrases.target: Laut Autor sei die Lage kritisch.
phrases.translation: According to the author the situation is critical.

phrases.target: Dennoch enthält der Artikel nützliche Daten.
phrases.translation: Nevertheless the article contains useful data.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: An fehlenden Quellen und emotionaler Sprache.

dialogue.speaker: Dozent
dialogue.target: Und wenn die Quelle anonym ist?
dialogue.translation: And if the source is anonymous?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Dann ist Vorsicht geboten; ich verifiziere separat.
dialogue.translation: Then caution is needed; I verify separately.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Screenshots ohne Kontext sind oft irreführend.
dialogue.translation: Screenshots without context are often misleading.

units.pragmatics: Distinguish Nachricht/Kommentar/Satire; cite primary sources.
units.culture: Public broadcasters and Correctiv/ARD Faktencheck are reference points.
units.speaking_prompt: Analyze a headline for bias and suggest verification steps.
units.writing_prompt: Write a short critical review of an online article.

checks.prompt: Was ist sinnvoll bei anonymen Quellen?

units.analogy: Media is like a lens: source, frame, and bias are the properties you inspect.
units.breakage: the lens analogy breaks with attributive participle constructions — die veröffentlichten Daten, der zitierte Bericht — because the sentence packs a whole clause into a noun phrase, and a lens stays flat while the German noun phrase folds information inside itself.

units.title: Migration, Identity, and Integration
units.scenario: You participate in a community forum on integration and belonging.
units.can_do: I can discuss migration experiences, identity, and integration policy thoughtfully.

phrases.target: Integration ist ein Prozess auf beiden Seiten.
phrases.translation: Integration is a process on both sides.

phrases.target: Ich fühle mich hier zunehmend zugehörig.
phrases.translation: I feel increasingly I belong here.

phrases.target: Sprache ist der Schlüssel zur Teilhabe.
Wie erleben Sie das in Ihrer Gemeinde?
phrases.translation: How do you experience that in your community?

dialogue.speaker: Moderator
dialogue.target: Was bedeutet Integration für Sie persönlich?
dialogue.translation: What does integration mean to you personally?

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Deutsch lernen, arbeiten und sozial mitmachen.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Offenheit und faire Chancen, nicht Assimilation um jeden Preis.
dialogue.translation: Openness and fair chances, not assimilation at any cost.

dialogue.speaker: Lernende
dialogue.target: Durch Begegnung, Bildung und ehrlichen Dialog.

units.pragmatics: Avoid stereotyping; use person-first sensitive language in public discourse.
units.culture: Einbürgerung rules reformed 2024; integration courses (Integrationskurs) are standard.
units.speaking_prompt: Share your integration experience or observations respectfully.
units.writing_prompt: Write a forum post on how language learning supports belonging.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Sprache ist der Schlüssel zur Teilhabe.' These?

units.analogy: Identity is like a mosaic: terms of belonging (Herkunft, Zugehörigkeit) are the tiles.
units.breakage: the mosaic analogy breaks with fixed prepositional frames — sich integrieren in + accusative, sich fühlen als — because each tile of belonging is glued with its own grammar, and the glue carries as much meaning as the tile.

units.title: Academic Writing and Essays
units.scenario: You draft a Hausarbeit introduction for a university Vorbereitungskurs.
units.can_do: I can structure academic texts with thesis, argumentation, citations, and register.

phrases.translation: In the following it is argued that …

phrases.target: Die Gliederung gliedert sich in drei Teile.
phrases.translation: The outline divides into three parts.

dialogue.speaker: Studierende
dialogue.target: Wie wirkt sich Homeoffice auf Teamkultur aus?
dialogue.translation: How does remote work affect team culture?

dialogue.speaker: Studierende
dialogue.target: Hybride Modelle können Kultur stärken, wenn Regeln klar sind.
dialogue.translation: Hybrid models can strengthen culture if rules are clear.

dialogue.speaker: Studierende
dialogue.target: Mit zwei Studien und einer Fallanalyse.
dialogue.translation: With two studies and a case analysis.

units.pragmatics: Academic German uses passive and nominalizations; avoid colloquialisms.
units.culture: Universities expect citation styles (APA/Chicago adapted); plagiarism serious.
units.speaking_prompt: Present thesis and outline orally for your paper topic.
units.writing_prompt: Write an introduction paragraph with thesis and roadmap.

checks.prompt: Sie lesen 'Im Folgenden wird argumentiert …' Register?

units.analogy: An essay is like an argument machine: thesis, development, conclusion — driven by nominal style and the passive.
units.breakage: the machine analogy breaks with connective grammar — dadurch, dass; indem — because one idea is subordinated under another, and subordination is a hierarchy the sequence-machine cannot represent.

units.title: Debates and Advanced Argumentation
units.scenario: You take part in a formal debate on climate policy measures.
units.can_do: I can build complex arguments, rebut opponents, and synthesize positions at CEFR B2 level.

phrases.target: Zum einen sparen wir CO₂, zum anderen entstehen Kosten.
phrases.translation: On one hand we save CO₂, on the other costs arise.

phrases.target: Unter dem Strich überwiegen die Vorteile.
phrases.translation: All in all the advantages outweigh.

phrases.target: Ich plädiere für einen schrittweisen Übergang.
phrases.translation: I plead for a gradual transition.

phrases.target: Können wir uns auf einen Kompromiss einigen?
phrases.translation: Can we agree on a compromise?

dialogue.speaker: Redner A
dialogue.translation: We need stricter CO₂ limits immediately.

dialogue.speaker: Redner B
dialogue.target: Mein Vorredner übersieht die sozialen Folgen.

dialogue.speaker: Redner A
dialogue.translation: Which consequences do you mean specifically?

dialogue.speaker: Redner B
dialogue.translation: Rising energy costs for low-income households.

dialogue.speaker: Redner A
dialogue.target: Dafür plädiere ich für gezielte Entlastungen.
dialogue.translation: For that I argue for targeted relief.

dialogue.speaker: Moderator
dialogue.target: Unter dem Strich: Tempo ja, aber sozial abfedern.
dialogue.translation: All in all: speed yes, but cushion socially.

units.pragmatics: Formal debate: address chair, timed turns, no personal attacks.
units.culture: Bundestag debates model formal argument; school Debattierclubs growing.
units.speaking_prompt: Deliver a 2-minute argument with one rebuttal and synthesis.
units.writing_prompt: Write a debate conclusion synthesizing both sides.

checks.prompt: Sie hören 'Können wir uns einigen?' Ziel?

units.analogy: Argumentation is like a chess match: claim, counter, concession — each move answered.
units.breakage: the chess analogy breaks with concession grammar — zwar ..., aber ... — which preserves the opponent's point while overturning it: chess captures pieces, German debates concede them before winning.
